title: bug: neither wrapper sends protectedEntries with record_candidate, so every verified-local qa_approve is refused protected-checks-unmeasured
description:
Found by the CQ-M07 final row's composed acceptance test (task-1a8f1d0e, step 1).
Evidence: record_candidate_rpc (scripts/moe-agent.sh:2724-2738) and Send-MoeCandidate (scripts/moe-agent.ps1:2168-2175) send {taskId, attemptId, generation, workerId, id, baseRevision, treeSha, deliveryTarget} and never protectedEntries; nothing else records it (grep -rn protectedEntries scripts/ outside tests: none). Under verified-local, check-dispatch.mjs owedChecks requires every owed check to carry dependencies, so a bare qualityGate stops with RUNNER_DEPENDENCIES_UNDECLARED and the task must declare executionContract.requiredChecks. Any declared requiredChecks makes policy.ts protectedCheckShortfall read the current candidate's protectedEntries; undefined gives protected-checks-unmeasured (policy.ts:400). So qa_approve on every verified-local task the real wrappers land is refused DELIVERY_EVIDENCE_MISSING [protected-checks-unmeasured], and a verified-local consumer is withheld the same way. The step-2 real-VM run (DoD 8) would fail at qa_approve.
Fix direction: in both wrappers' frozen-candidate record, send protectedEntries = the `git ls-tree -r -z --full-tree <M> -- <protected paths>` blob entries ({path, oid}, byte-sorted, at most 2000) for the paths under the task's approved requiredCheckSnapshot definitions (configs, scripts, assertionRoots; get_context task.executionContract.requiredChecks), only when requiredChecks is declared; omit it otherwise (legacy byte-identical). Keep sh/ps1 parity.
definitionOfDone: Under a task whose executionContract declares requiredChecks, both moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 record the frozen candidate with protectedEntries equal to the merged tree's blob entries under the definitions' configs, scripts and assertionRoots (sorted by path bytes, exactly {path, oid}); a postflight-vm-route row per wrapper pins the payload against a fake daemon.
A task without requiredChecks (and every legacy/observe task) sends a record_candidate payload byte-identical to today's; a row pins it in both wrappers.
A protected path with no blob in the merged tree is omitted from protectedEntries (the daemon reports protected-check-changed for it), never invented; tested.
parity-check.sh, parity-check.ps1 and npm run lint pass; the gate stays within 20 minutes.
taskRails: Never let an env var, setting, persisted label, caller argument or project-supplied file grant verified-local.
Legacy, the default, stays byte-for-byte unchanged in behavior.

implementationPlan.note: FAKE_CTX_CONTRACT on the task-scoped get_context (jsonKnob; a non-object throws; unset serves no field). candidateReply runs protectedEntriesCheck (readProtectedEntries rules, plus normalizedPath mirroring normalizeAffectedFile, drive letter included) only when args.protectedEntries !== undefined; a violation throws inside evidenceRpc's try, so the wrapper gets FIXTURE_REFUSED. Smoke: absent, [] and a byte-sorted list are accepted; a mis-sorted list, an extra key, leading whitespace, a bad oid, null and 'a//b' are each refused; the contract is served only when set.

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/moe-agent.sh, plus its rows in scripts/tests/postflight-vm-route.sh. Read mem:gotcha-verified-local-protected-entries first. Edit only with the Edit tool.

WRAPPER: add a new helper, protected_entries_json (Twin: Get-MoeProtectedEntries), called only from record_candidate_rpc after both attempt checks pass.
1. Profile gate first: continue only when strong_landing_task "$LAND_TASK_ID" succeeds. Otherwise nothing new runs (no context parse, no git), and the same python builds args into today's JSON bytes in today's key order: taskId, attemptId, generation, workerId, id, baseRevision, treeSha, deliveryTarget.
2. Contract: read PREFLIGHT_CONTEXT from python's stdin, never argv (FAKE_CTX_PAD_BYTES rows push it past 128 KiB). Use it only when it parses as an object whose task.id equals LAND_TASK_ID. requiredChecks count as declared only when task.executionContract.requiredChecks is a non-empty list. A missing, foreign or unparseable context, or no list, keeps today's payload and prints no warning; the daemon then judges.
3. Paths: the de-duplicated union of every definition's configs, scripts and assertionRoots. If there are no paths, send protectedEntries [] and do NOT call git: ls-tree with no pathspec lists the whole tree.
4. Measure the candidate's own tree with git -C "$MOE_TOP" --literal-pathspecs ls-tree -r -z --full-tree "$FROZEN_TREE" -- <paths>, run through subprocess with an argv list. Keep the records with mode 100644, 100755 or 120000 and type blob, as {"path": p, "oid": o} in that key order, sorted by path.encode('utf-8'). A protected path with no blob is simply absent (DoD 3); never fill it from the approved snapshot or the base.
5. Unmeasurable: omit the field. Never invent an entry and never send a partial list. Check records in git order; the first offender names the reason:
- 'requiredChecks unreadable': a definition is not an object with string-list paths;
- 'git ls-tree failed': a non-zero exit, or python itself failing;
- 'non-blob entry': for example a 160000 gitlink;
- 'unsupported path': not strict UTF-8, or a path the daemon refuses (a control character, a backslash, leading or trailing whitespace, over 500 characters);
- 'more than 2000 entries': checked after parsing.
Then print exactly one line to stderr with printf (mem:gotcha-launcher-user-path-strings), byte-identical to the ps1 twin:
[WARN] record_candidate: the protected check files of task <taskId> were not measured on tree <tree> (<reason>); the candidate is recorded without protectedEntries, so qa_approve will report protected-checks-unmeasured.
6. args gains protectedEntries as its LAST key, and only when step 3 or 4 produced a list. moe_evidence_rpc's acknowledgement (a type-checked python ==) already refuses an echo that drops or changes it.
Error handling: no branch can grant anything; an omitted or wrong list only makes qa_approve refuse. The helper never fails the candidate record or the landing.

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/moe-agent.ps1 twin of step 2, plus its rows in scripts/tests/postflight-vm-route.ps1. Keep moe-agent.ps1 UTF-8 with BOM, and edit it only with the Edit tool.

WRAPPER:
- Add a new helper, Get-MoeProtectedEntries $Git $TaskId $Tree (Twin: protected_entries_json). It uses step 2's exact rules, reasons and [WARN] bytes, printed with Write-Host -ForegroundColor Yellow.
- Profile gate first: Test-MoeStrongLandingTask $TaskId $Git.GitDir.
- Context: $preflightContext, used only when its task.id -ceq $TaskId. Read the definitions with Get-MoeProp, and wrap each list in @(), because a one-item list unrolls.
- git: Invoke-MoeGit -Top $Git.Top -GitArgs (@('--literal-pathspecs','ls-tree','-r','-z','--full-tree',$Tree,'--') + $paths). Split the output with ((Out -join "`n").Split([char]0)), as the wrapper does elsewhere. Match each record with '^(100644|100755|120000) blob ([0-9a-f]{40})\t([\s\S]+)$'. A decoded path that holds U+FFFD is 'unsupported path', matching sh's strict decode.
- Sort by UTF-8 bytes with a [Collections.Generic.List[...]] .Sort([Comparison[...]]{...}) that compares, with [string]::CompareOrdinal, the hex of each path's UTF-8 bytes. Probed: this works on 5.1 and 7 (mem:gotcha-ps1-byte-order-sort-and-array-ack). Never use Sort-Object: it is culture-aware and case-blind. Never use [Array]::Sort(keys, items, comparer): called from PowerShell it left the items unsorted.
- Build entries as [ordered]@{ path = ...; oid = ... }. Return them inside a wrapper object (e.g. @{ Entries = ... }) or as $null, so a 0- or 1-entry list never unrolls through the return.
- Send-MoeCandidate gains a $Git parameter. Its three callers pass their $Git: the shared-mode landing (~6201), the strong worktree L6 (~7451) and the legacy worktree L6 (~7459). Build the legacy hashtable exactly as today, and add protectedEntries = @(...) only when a list was measured.
- Leave Send-MoeEvidence unchanged. Its per-key compare already acknowledges echoes of 0, 1 and 2 entries on both engines (probed).
Error handling: as in step 2, every failure omits the field and prints one WARN, and nothing here fails the record or the landing. A throw inside the helper is caught and counts as 'git ls-tree failed'.

ROWS, the twins of step 2's rows in Invoke-SgRows / Assert-SgRow:
- The PE fixture, as a $script:VmrSetup variant: Initialize-SgFixture, then the same files and commit. Build the non-ASCII name from [char]0xE9, never a literal. Add the gitlink when PE_GITLINK is set. Then run branch -f main and update $script:VmjBase.
- FAKE_CTX_CONTRACT on SG-legacy and SG-observe.
- PE-pass, PE-empty and PE-unmeasured.
- In Assert-SgRow's payload expectation, compare the record_candidate argument names as a sorted set: a ps1 @{} has no stable key order in pwsh 7, so 'today' means the same 8 names and values with no protectedEntries. Compare the protectedEntries entries in order, each as the exact JSON {"path":..,"oid":..}.
- Restore $script:VmrSetup and $script:VmjBase before Invoke-SrRows.
Iterate with the ps1 slice from mem:pattern-vm-route-strong-receipt-slice, run from a /mnt/d cwd with the env scrubbed and WSLENV=MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC, on both engines:

implementationPlan.note: moe-agent.ps1 (BOM kept, ef bb bf): new Get-MoeProtectedEntries, the twin of protected_entries_json, with the same rules, reasons and WARN bytes. It is gated first on Test-MoeStrongLandingTask and reads $preflightContext only when task.id -ceq the TaskId. The definitions are read through a local raw-property scriptblock instead of Get-MoeProp, so that a one-item list stays a list and a bare string is refused. An empty-string path is 'requiredChecks unreadable', because 5.1 drops empty native args and ls-tree would then list the whole tree. git runs as Invoke-MoeGit --literal-pathspecs ls-tree -r -z --full-tree inside try/catch, and the trailing NUL is checked with the Ordinal EndsWith. Entries are sorted with a List.Sort Comparison by CompareOrdinal over the hex of the UTF-8 bytes, as [ordered]@{path;oid}, and returned in @{Entries=...}. Send-MoeCandidate gains $Git; all 3 callers pass it, and the legacy hashtable is unchanged. postflight-vm-route.ps1: Initialize-PeFixture ([char]0xE9, $script:PeGitlink), FAKE_CTX_CONTRACT on SG-legacy/SG-observe, and PE-pass/PE-unmeasured/PE-empty. Assert-SgRow gains Payload/Paths: the arg names are compared as an ordinal-sorted set, each entry as exact path,oid against `git rev-parse M:path`, and the WARN line exactly. Evidence: ParseFile shows 0 errors on 5.1 and 7 for both files. The slice (Invoke-SgRows only, scratch snapshot) gives SLICE-OK EXIT=0 on pwsh 7 and on 5.1. executionContract.intendedBehavior: On a strong (verified-local) landing whose task's executionContract declares requiredChecks, moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 record the frozen candidate with protectedEntries: the candidate tree's blob entries under every definition's configs, scripts and assertionRoots, as exact {path, oid} objects in UTF-8 byte order ([] when the definitions name no path). qa_approve can then compare them with the approved requiredCheckSnapshot instead of refusing protected-checks-unmeasured. Every other landing (legacy, observe, or strong without requiredChecks) sends today's record_candidate payload unchanged. A tree whose protected entries cannot be measured faithfully (a non-blob entry, more than 2000 entries, a path the daemon would refuse, a git failure) is recorded without the field and with one [WARN] line, so the daemon fails closed; nothing is invented.
acceptanceCriteria: PE-pass, in postflight-vm-route.sh and in postflight-vm-route.ps1 on 5.1 and 7: the record_candidate args end with protectedEntries for package-lock.json, scripts/lint.sh, tests/B.txt, 'tests/a b.txt', tests/a.txt, tests/sub/c.txt, tests/<U+00E9>.txt and vm-job.txt, in that order. Each oid equals git rev-parse <treeSha>:<path>, and each entry is exactly {path, oid}. scripts/gone.sh (no blob), scripts/other.sh, unprotected.txt and seed.txt are absent. main moves to C.

Strong without requiredChecks (SG-pass and every refused SG row) and legacy/observe with requiredChecks (SG-legacy, SG-observe): the record_candidate args are exactly today's 8 keys (sh in today's order), there is no protectedEntries, and no protected-entries [WARN] line is printed.
PE-empty: a strong task whose requiredChecks name no path records protectedEntries: [], and git never lists the whole tree.

PE-unmeasured: a gitlink under a protected root leaves the payload at today's 8 keys and prints exactly one '[WARN] record_candidate: the protected check files of task task-postflight were not measured on tree <treeSha> (non-blob entry); ...' line. The landing still lands.
The fake daemon refuses a protectedEntries list that breaks packages/moe-daemon/src/state/candidateStore.ts readProtectedEntries, so a mis-sorted or malformed list turns its row red.
invariants: Only strong_landing_task / Test-MoeStrongLandingTask decide strong, from wrapper- or daemon-written records. No env var, setting, CLI-written file or caller argument decides strong or the protected paths.

protectedEntries are measured on exactly the candidate's own treeSha (FROZEN_TREE / $Frozen.Tree), never filled from the approved snapshot or the base. When in doubt the field is omitted, which can only make qa_approve refuse.
git ls-tree never runs without a pathspec. Pathspecs are literal (--literal-pathspecs) and passed after --, through an argv list, never a shell string.
The [WARN] line is byte-identical in both wrappers, and moe-agent.ps1 stays UTF-8 with BOM.
compatibility: Legacy and observe landings, and strong landings without requiredChecks, send the same record_candidate payload as today: in sh the JSON is byte-identical in today's key order, and in ps1 the same 8 keys and values. Those paths add no RPC, git call or context parse.

The record_candidate wire contract is unchanged. protectedEntries is the optional field docs/MCP_SERVER.md already defines: omit it when not measured; [] means nothing exists under those paths. There is no daemon, check-dispatch, journal or landing-order change.
The fake daemon's new knob and validation are inert for every suite that sends no protectedEntries: the postflight.{sh,ps1} frozen modes, postflight-worktree.cjs and the other vm-route sections.

That is unchanged behavior, and a separate human decision if it is ever wanted.
- A fresh unserved get_context at landing: rejected in favour of the pre-flight read both wrappers already hold. That read adds no RPC (existing call-log rows stay unchanged) and is guaranteed in worktree mode.
- Failing the landing when entries cannot be measured: rejected in favour of omitting the field and printing one WARN. The doc contract says 'omit when not measured'. The daemon then refuses approval, nothing is invented, and there is no new landing failure mode or unlanded route.
- A shared node helper (.mjs) for both wrappers: rejected. It needs IDE bundle wiring and a sixth file.
- Reading .moe/tasks/<id>.json directly: rejected, because get_context is the daemon-owned read.
- Hardening Send-MoeEvidence for arrays: not needed. A probe showed today's per-key compare already handles 0, 1 and 2 entries on 5.1 and 7 (mem:gotcha-ps1-byte-order-sort-and-array-ack).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- record_candidate_rpc / Send-MoeCandidate is the only place that records a candidate, for both shared-mode and worktree landings. Adding the field there covers both modes.
- The worktree strong L6 (sh ~7822, ps1 ~7447) already evaluates strong_landing_task before freeze_candidate. The legacy L6 and the shared landing reach the same function with strong false.
- FROZEN_TREE / $Frozen.Tree is the candidate's treeSha (M in worktree mode).
- git ls-tree -r prints full paths in byte order, because git sorts tree entries with a '/' appended to directory names. The explicit sort is a safeguard, and the PE-pass row pins it: tests/B.txt < 'tests/a b.txt' < tests/a.txt.
- Invoke-MoeGit sets the console output encoding to UTF-8. PowerShell splits native output on newlines, so the wrapper rejoins with a newline and splits on [char]0.
- In pwsh 7, @{} key order varies per process, so ps1 payload rows compare key SETS.
- The fake seat's VM job adds vm-job.txt to M, which lets the rows prove the entries come from M rather than B.
- The daemon-side acceptance row L3(e) (task-1a8f1d0e) pins the daemon's fail-closed refusal of a candidate without protectedEntries. It stays valid after this wrapper fix.
- Under verified-local, check-dispatch needs requiredChecks: a bare qualityGate gives RUNNER_DEPENDENCIES_UNDECLARED. That is why every real verified-local task hits this path.
planningNotes.risks:
- Do NOT declare executionContract.requiredChecks on this task. The repo runs legacy, which by DoD 2 still omits the field, so this task's own qa_approve would refuse protected-checks-unmeasured.
- PowerShell unrolling: a function returning a 0- or 1-item array hands back $null or the bare item. Wrap collections in @() where they are used, and return the entries inside a wrapper object.
- Never use Sort-Object or [Array]::Sort(keys, items) for byte order: a probe showed both get it wrong.
- On Windows a very long pathspec list can pass the 32K command-line limit. That surfaces as 'git ls-tree failed' (field omitted, one WARN), never as a wrong list.
- The gitlink fixture: tests/mod is an empty directory in W, which is normal. If provisioning or the fake seat trips on it, trigger the unmeasured path with more than 2000 blobs under tests/ instead, and say so in the summary.
- Non-ASCII file name: in sh build it from bytes (printf '\303\251'); in ps1 from [char]0xE9. Never use a literal, which PS 5.1 can misread.
- SG-legacy and SG-observe are host-gate controls. Adding FAKE_CTX_CONTRACT must not change their kind or their other assertions.
- The new WARN must never appear on a legacy row; sg_check's default 'today' asserts this.
- Gate time: the dry run took 514 s at load ~2. The new rows add about 1-3 min, well inside the 20-minute rail.
- No other open task declares these five files (checked 2026-11-05: only a251cd63, which is JetBrains-only, and the BLOCKED final task).
